title: Standardize floating-label behavior and error animation across form inputs
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Background: Our form components (text fields, selects, toggles) currently use inconsistent floating label behavior and error state animations across platforms and break at small sizes. This causes a maintenance burden for engineering and causes flicker/shift regressions in product pages. Goal: Define a single, accessible floating-label pattern and a lightweight error/validation animation that works across dense, regular, and large density tokens and that integrates with existing color and motion token sets. Scope: text fields (single-line, multi-line), native-looking selects (single and multi), toggle/switch focus and invalid states. Exclusions: full redesign of input visuals, internationalization edge-cases for RTL will be handled in a follow-up ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Figma spec with token mappings for floating-label positions (rest, floated, collapsed) for three density scales
Motion spec with 2-step animation (label lift + subtle underline pulse) under 120ms total, with reduced-motion alternative
Accessibility checklist: label association (for attribute), error text announced by screen readers, 4.5:1 contrast for error text and 3:1 for helper text
Engineers have a clear mapping table: component prop -> visual variant -> token names
Design tokens updated: label-transform, label-scale, input-underline-thickness, error-color, motion-ease, motion-duration
Consolidated unit test/visual regression checklist added to the ticket and linked PRs
decisions: Use a single floating-label baseline: 12px vertical lift with 0.92x font-scale when floated for dense and 0.85x for regular
Error animation limited to underline color fade + 6px subtle shake for 80ms for micro-interactions; provide reduced-motion variant that only changes color
Prefer tokenized motion values (motion-duration-fast, motion-ease-standard) instead of hard-coded numbers in code
Label remains visually present (not removed) on focus and on invalid to aid discoverability
Avoid using transform translateZ hacks that cause blur on some GPUs; prefer translateY and opacity only
